accuracy.why: Every element of the English body is in the Urdu and nothing is added: «سر اٹھائے کھڑا ہے» (rises), «چھوتے چھوتے رہ جاتی ہیں» (almost brushes), «دنیا کا سب سے بڑا نخلستان» (in the world, as the Arabic and the site rule have it, with no palm and no natural in that sentence), warmth tied to «عین سردیوں میں» and never to night. Two points off for two approximations: «قدرتی خوبی» is neither the English wonder nor the Arabic phenomenon but a word between them, and faq[2].q «کس وجہ سے مشہور ہیں؟» moves «mild temperature» out of the question and leaves it in the answer. The English-only «heritage village» is absent by the Arabic-authority rule, not by error (P15).

nativeness.why: The body now reads as Urdu written from the start: «جب گرمی عروج پر ہو تو», «راہداریوں سے گزریں تو … پھر اچانک راستہ … ہال میں جا نکلتا ہے», «باریک کرن», beside what the reader had already praised («کسی قدیم نگہبان کی طرح سر اٹھائے کھڑا ہے», «کھجور کے درختوں کا سمندر»). Four points off for what a reader will still catch: the clock in «روزانہ 8:00–22:00» and «8:00 سے 22:00 تک», which he converts in his head (kept provisional, P13); the Good-for row «کس کے لیے موزوں … گرم دن»; the kicker «ارضیاتی عجوبہ», exact but stiff; a fee cell that carries a name he cannot place plus a parenthesis; and the fact that the twenty edits of this stage, though mostly in the reader's own words, have not themselves been read blind.

compliance.why: Names are byte-identical to the termbase keys («جبل القارہ» x6, «الاحساء» x4, «ہفوف» x1, «ارض الحضارات» x2); every agreement the edits touch was re-read («والے ہال میں», «باریک کرن … آتی ہے», «قدرتی خوبی کی وجہ سے», «غار ہیں», «گرمی عروج پر ہو»); the scan of all 29 strings finds no Arabic letterform, no non-Latin digit, no Latin letter, no izafat sign and no stray punctuation. One point off because two forms on the page are still provisional (the head-name spelling and the clock form) and the entries «الاحساء» and «ارض الحضارات» stay pending; one point off because «ہال» enters on a headword and a corpus count rather than a printed gender label, and because the edited text has passed this stage's own scan only: stage45-check.mjs still encodes three rules this run replaced (currency, the Jabal gloss, the token «تو»).

fit.why: For this reader: the price in his own words with no Latin code («بڑوں کے لیے 50 سعودی ریال»), the oasis named at first mention («الاحساء کے نخلستان»), the Urdu generic «پہاڑ» in place of a bracket, a meaning gloss on «ارض الحضارات», an FAQ that now answers the question it asks. Against: he still cannot tell what «ارض الحضارات» is or whether he can buy at the gate (P15, the owner's), and he still meets «22:00» (P13, the owner's). The empty best time, the missing child price and the unnamed holidays are the source's and are charged here only as the half point by which the page, as he meets it, is thinner than he needs.

structure.why: Same 29 leaf paths as stage 5 and the pack, in the same order; the body is one plain-text paragraph with no Markdown, link or line break; «{op}» stands once in det.hoursNotice and not in det.hoursNotice.op; det.openMaps keeps its trailing « ↗»; no heading, label or title carries a stop or a bracket; the twenty changes replay exactly from the stage-5 fields to these.

blind_reader_rulings.reason: P3a (gloss of a generic inside a name). Ruled there and applied: the bracket «(القارہ پہاڑ)» is removed. «جبل» is an Urdu dictionary word (Rekhta: جبل, اسم مذکر: پہاڑ), the bracket explained the one word the reader knew and for a moment read as a second name, and the text says «پہاڑ» two sentences later. His other wish, help with saying «القارہ», is not met: as written it reads al-Qara, which is the Arabic (no doubled r); a Latin or vowelled gloss would break the naming policy to state what the spelling already gives.

The oasis is named at its first mention in the body: «الاحساء کے نخلستان کے بیچوں بیچ». Not a new fact — the same paragraph's last sentence, the area line and answer_en identify it, and the approved zh line anchors it at this spot. The summary stays as it is: it also serves the home-page card, and the source summary names nothing.

Diagnosis accepted (a cave does not «بل کھاتا»; «بیچ» echoed «بیچوں بیچ»): «چٹانوں میں غار ہیں اور راستے بل کھاتے چلے گئے ہیں۔». His exact wording was not used, because «ان کے درمیان» would say the passages run between the caves, which the source does not state and the Arabic body speaks against.

All three phrases replaced with his wording, in the body (change 3) and in faq[2].a (change 16): «جب گرمی عروج پر ہو تو», «عین سردیوں میں», «ہلکی سی گرمائش». The Arabic itself says the peak of the heat («ذروة القيظ»). Warmth stays on the season word «سردیوں» (C16). Stage 2's removal of the adverb «عین» is ruled under P18.

(a) Register: «قدرتی مظہر کے باعث» becomes «قدرتی خوبی کی وجہ سے» — his noun and postposition, with «قدرتی» kept because both sources say natural. (b) «Shelter from what, and do they still?» is the source's own silence («to shelter here since antiquity», «يأوون إليها منذ القِدم»): adding «گرمی اور سردی سے» would add; logged as source defect SD8.
His join is taken: «راہداریوں سے گزریں تو … رہ جاتی ہیں، پھر اچانک …». The verb stays honorific; a command becomes «when you pass», as in the approved zh line.

All three points: «ایوان» to «ہال» (palace hall / parliament; Urdu Lughat headword ہال: بڑا کمرہ، بڑا دالان; decision recorded under P16), «میں کھل جاتا ہے» to «میں جا نکلتا ہے», «لکیر» to «کرن». «چھن کر آتی ہے» stays, as in his own rewrite: the source names no opening for the light, so none is supplied.

The English body goes from the chamber to the summit in consecutive sentences (it compresses a four-paragraph Arabic body) and neither source says whether or how a visitor reaches the top. Nothing is added. SD1.

Both sources say the view «sums up why Al-Ahsa became» the largest oasis («يلخّص لماذا صارت»); the Urdu says what they say. His «کیوں کہا جاتا ہے» is not taken: it would turn a claim the Arabic states flatly into a reported one. SD2.
Order reversed to his wording, «الاحساء میں، ہفوف کے مشرق میں», and ruled as the pattern for every area line (P20). That the line gives a direction and no distance is the source's (SD10).

«During the daytime.» / «فترة النهار.» is all the source gives, beside a 22:00 closing time; the information he misses cannot be supplied. SD3. Two points that are the Urdu's: the «وقت … وقت» echo is removed («دن میں۔», change 8); the final «۔» stays, because the source value is a sentence with a stop in all five languages — a data matter for every language or none.

P13, the clock form — one of the two provisional decisions the owner has not approved. Not ruled here; the 24-hour form stays in the text and my recommendation (his own «صبح 8 بجے سے رات 10 بجے تک») is in the calibration list with the strings each option changes.

Which holidays, and until when, the source does not say («on holidays», «في العطلات», «may be extended»). SD4. The idiom he names is applied in both places (changes 9 and 12): «زیادہ دیر تک کھلا رہ سکتا ہے» — «تک» added, «زیادہ» kept because «extended» is a comparison with the normal closing time.

(b) «بالغوں» becomes «بڑوں» in the card and the answer (changes 10 and 13). (c) The Latin code goes under P7, which is ruled (change 11). (a) A child price is not in the source, which gives the adult price only: SD5.

P15, what «ارض الحضارات» is — the English says heritage village, the Arabic field the bare name, the Arabic body a project. A fact about a third party on which the sources differ: the owner's (SD6). The bare name stays. The meaning gloss stays too (P3b, ruled): his reading of «حضارات» as «حضرات» is the misreading it is there to catch.

Four points. Label: no wording was offered and the neutral alternatives are worse («موزوں برائے» is signboard Persian, bare «موزوں» a truncation); the mismatch is the source row's, which lists an audience, an activity and a kind of weather under one preposition (SD9; ruled under P21). «فیملی» and «فوٹوگرافی»: English loans where a common Urdu word stands — style_rules.anglicisms, a termbase rule that a register preference does not overrule (P16); «بال بچوں کے ساتھ» is not a «who» either and assumes the reader is a family head. «گرم دن» underselling: the source row says hot days only.

Two parts. «No way to confirm»: an artifact of the plain-text copy he read — on the page this word is the link to the operator's account; nothing is missing. Bare «انتظامیہ» reading as the district administration: real; his fix names the page, which a string shared by all pages cannot, so the same possessor is given generically, «وہاں کی انتظامیہ» (the management there). UI string: carried to the ui.ur batch.
«گوگل میپس پر دیکھیں ↗», his wording. UI string: carried to the ui.ur batch.
P7, currency form. Ruled there and applied: «50 SAR» becomes «50 سعودی ریال», the same form as the card. The child price and the identity of «ارض الحضارات» are as under 14 and 15.

The question no longer carries its own answer: «جبل القارہ کے غار کس وجہ سے مشہور ہیں؟» (his first remedy; the approved Russian line did the same). The answer is reworded with observation 4 (change 16). The circular question is in the English, Arabic and Chinese fields: SD7. One claim of his is not adopted as stated — that «کے لیے مشہور» is un-Urdu: ur.wikipedia has it 2892 times against 611 for «کی وجہ سے مشہور»; the reframing makes the point moot.
Grammar: «کون سا وقت؟» is answered by «دن کا وقت۔». That the answer says no more is the source's (SD3).

«قدرت کا عجوبہ» would erase a distinction the Arabic makes: the kicker's only source is «أعجوبة جيولوجية», and zh, de and ru all keep geological; «ارضیاتی» is the Urdu word for it. Two labels for one place are by design (category and kicker). «فطرت» against «قدرت» for the category label is a UI string that has to be chosen with the other category labels and the header-fit measurement: carried to the ui.ur batch with his candidate, not changed here.

fields.body: الاحساء کے نخلستان کے بیچوں بیچ جبل القارہ کسی قدیم نگہبان کی طرح سر اٹھائے کھڑا ہے، مگر اس کا راز بلندی میں نہیں، اس کے اندر چھپا ہے۔ چٹانوں میں غار ہیں اور راستے بل کھاتے چلے گئے ہیں۔ جب گرمی عروج پر ہو تو ان میں خوشگوار ٹھنڈک رہتی ہے، اور عین سردیوں میں ہلکی سی گرمائش۔ اسی قدرتی خوبی کی وجہ سے الاحساء کے لوگ قدیم زمانے سے یہاں پناہ لیتے آئے ہیں۔ پہاڑ کی تنگ راہداریوں سے گزریں تو چٹانیں کندھوں کو چھوتے چھوتے رہ جاتی ہیں، پھر اچانک راستہ اونچی چھت والے ہال میں جا نکلتا ہے، جہاں روشنی کی ایک باریک کرن چھن کر آتی ہے۔ چوٹی سے نخلستان یوں پھیلا دکھائی دیتا ہے جیسے کھجور کے درختوں کا سمندر ہو۔ یہی ایک منظر بتا دیتا ہے کہ الاحساء دنیا کا سب سے بڑا نخلستان کیوں بنا۔

changes.why: Calibration P3a (blind-reader observation 1): the bracketed gloss is removed. «جبل» is an Urdu dictionary word (Rekhta: جبل, اسم مذکر: پہاڑ، کوہ); the reader, unprompted, said the bracket explained the one word he already knew and for a moment read it as a second name, and the page itself says «پہاڑ» two sentences later. With the bracket gone the name would abut «نخلستان» and could be read as one name («جبل القارہ نخلستان»), so the locative is moved in front of the subject, which is also the ordinary Urdu order. No word of the source is lost.

The reader's own wording was not taken whole: «ان کے درمیان راستے» would say the passages run between the caves, a relation the source does not state (the Arabic body says the mountain has no single connected passage). changes.why: Observation 4: the three phrases the reader heard as translated are replaced by his wording. In Urdu it is the heat that is «عروج پر», which is also what the Arabic authority says («في ذروة القيظ», the peak of the heat); «عین سردیوں میں» is the idiom for the depth of winter and keeps the season word, so warmth stays tied to winter (site rule C16); «ہلکی سی» is the collocate of «گرمائش» where «دھیمی» belongs to sound, flame and speed. Stage 2 had removed «عین» to keep the adverb away from the generic «عین» of later spring names: ruled under P18 as a page-level guard, not a site-wide ban.

calibration.question: A generic inside a compound name («جبل», later «عین», «قصر», «سوق»): translated, or transliterated with a gloss?
candidates: A — name transliterated whole, the generic glossed once in a bracket as a second name form: «جبل القارہ (القارہ پہاڑ)» (the stage 1–5 text)
B — the generic translated in running text («القارہ پہاڑ»), «جبل القارہ» as title only
C — a sentence gloss: «عربی میں “جبل” پہاڑ کو کہتے ہیں»
D — the Persian generic: «کوہ القارہ»
E — no bracket where the generic is itself an Urdu word; the Urdu generic stands alone in the body (this ruling)
calibration.evidence: For keeping «جبل» inside the name: ur.wikipedia «جبل احد» 305 against «کوہ احد» 8 and «احد پہاڑ» 10, «جبل رحمت» 73 against 0, «جبل طویق» 6 against 0 (stage 4, from its logs); Urdu News keeps «جبل» in every mountain name and never writes «کوہ» (0 in 11 pages). For a bracket: Urdu News does paraphrase with «<name> پہاڑ» («حرفۃ پہاڑ», «المنجور پہاڑ», «القارۃ پہاڑ»), and de and ru gloss at this spot. Against the bracket on this page: the blind reader, unprompted (observation 1): it «explains the one word I already knew», and «القارہ پہاڑ is not how Urdu forms a mountain name»; asked afterwards: «for a split second I did wonder whether it was meant as the name people use in Urdu» and «it also turned out not to be needed», because the text says «پہاڑ» two sentences later. Rekhta, read in this run: «جَبَل — اسم، مذکر — پہاڑ، کوہ، پربت». Stages 1 and 3 had themselves noted that for this reader the gloss «confirms rather than explains» and earns its place «mainly by fixing the pattern» for later generics: a gloss kept for the pipeline, not for the reader.
calibration.ruling_or_recommendation: Three parts. (1) The name is transliterated whole, in the title and in the text; the generic inside it is never translated as part of the name and never doubled («جبل القارہ پہاڑ» stays forbidden). (2) The gloss is owed by need, not by reflex. A generic that is an Urdu dictionary word in the same sense takes no bracket; «جبل» is one. Instead the Urdu generic «پہاڑ» stands alone at least once in the body, away from the name, so that the page says in Urdu what the thing is — that is the gloss. (3) Where the reader's unprompted reaction and gloss_regel as written disagree, I follow the reader: the rule was inherited from three lines in whose languages «Jabal» is opaque, and its purpose, that no transliterated word is left unexplained, is met here by the word being Urdu already. gloss_regel is amended to «once per term whose generic is not an Urdu word in that sense». The form of the gloss for a generic that is opaque is not settled by this page: P3c.
calibration.binds: Every page whose title carries «جبل» (the other mountains of Al-Ahsa), and the principle (gloss by need) for every compound name on the 58 pages.
calibration.guard: Stage-5 item 10 and the stage checker: (a) no «(» directly after a name that begins «جبل »; (b) on a page whose title begins «جبل », the token «پہاڑ» occurs at least once in the body and never next to the name; (c) the title never carries a bracket.
